newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch Group ING discussing purchase of Dillon Read.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Group ING discussing purchase of Dillon Read.

text.p: Dutch financial services group ING Groep NV, is in talks that may lead to its buying U.S. investment bank Dillon, Read & Co.

Ing spokesman Ruud Polet said ING was in talks to either buy the balance outstanding of the privately-owned bank or sell the 25 percent stake held by its ING Barings investment banking arm under an option that expires July 1.
He said the talks should be completed within a couple weeks.
"If the conditions are right for both parties, it would be nice to have it all," Polet told Reuters.
He declined to comment on a report in London's Evening Standard newspaper that ING Barings would pay between $425 million and $450 million for the remaining 75 percent.
He said the talks with Dillon Read were mainly about price but dealt also with other issues.
"Of course it would be nice to have an investment bank in the U.S. There are so many opportunities," Polet added.
The New York-based firm has a good presence in mergers and acquisitions for mid-market companies and this has helped ING Barings' own corporate finance operation in London, bankers said.
ING Barings already employs around 1,200 people in New York, specialising in global high yield businesses, emerging markets and banking.
